citations.description: Evidence summary states: 'TicketTransport.add_label: Implemented in transport.py at line 238–239, but no live test exercises it. SupportsLinks methods: set_relationship and get_issuelinks_map are implemented in transport.py (lines 253–263), but neither is called in any live test. map_remote_links and link_payload_for_relation are part of the SupportsLinks Protocol (lines 232–247) but are not implemented in JiraDataCenterTransport at all, and have no live test coverage.'

findings.detail: The evidence explicitly identifies gaps: `TicketTransport.add_label` has no live test. All four `SupportsLinks` protocol methods (`set_relationship`, `get_issuelinks_map`, `map_remote_links`, `link_payload_for_relation`) have no live test coverage, and `map_remote_links` and `link_payload_for_relation` are not implemented in the transport at all. The operator-attested ticket comment does not claim coverage for these methods.
findings.remediation: Add live tests against the J5 harness for `add_label`, `set_relationship`, `get_issuelinks_map`, `map_remote_links`, and `link_payload_for_relation`. Implement the missing `map_remote_links` and `link_payload_for_relation` methods in `JiraDataCenterTransport`. Record the passing run output in a ticket comment explicitly enumerating all protocol methods.
findings.title: Missing live test coverage for add_label and all SupportsLinks methods

findings.criterion: `pip install nava-rebar` then `pip show jira` reports not-installed, and `import rebar` succeeds
findings.detail: The evidence for this criterion is incomplete — the evidence text ends mid-sentence ('Now let me check the test that specifically covers the `import rebar` without jira installed:') with no actual findings reported. No test file, no pyproject.toml evidence, and no CI output demonstrating this behavior was provided.
findings.remediation: Provide evidence: (1) pyproject.toml showing `jira` is not in the base dependencies, (2) a test or CI step that installs `nava-rebar` without extras, runs `pip show jira` and asserts not-installed, then asserts `import rebar` succeeds.
findings.title: No evidence that `pip install nava-rebar` excludes jira and `import rebar` still succeeds

findings.criterion: importing the DC transport without the extra raises an error naming `pip install nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]`
findings.detail: The evidence text ends with 'Let me check if there's a test for this in the main transport test file or elsewhere:' — no actual findings were reported. No test demonstrating the missing-extra error message was identified.
findings.remediation: Provide evidence of a test that imports the DC transport without the `[jira-datacenter]` extra installed and asserts the resulting error message names `pip install nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]`.
findings.title: No evidence of a test asserting the missing-extra error message

findings.criterion: a malformed `[tool.rebar.jira]` config raises `ConfigError` rather than falling back to env-only
findings.detail: The evidence text ends with 'Now I have a complete picture. Let me also check if there's a specific test for the DC settings' fail-loud behavior:' — no actual findings were reported. No test or code demonstrating that a malformed config raises `ConfigError` (rather than silently falling back to env-only) was identified.
findings.remediation: Provide evidence of a test that supplies a malformed `[tool.rebar.jira]` section and asserts `ConfigError` is raised rather than a silent env-only fallback.
findings.title: No evidence of ConfigError on malformed [tool.rebar.jira] config

findings.criterion: the DC backend REJECTS a non-`https` `reconciler.base_url` with a `ConfigError` naming the cleartext
findings.detail: The evidence text ends with 'The held-out test file doesn't contain a test for the non-`https` rejection. Let me search more specifically for that test.' — no actual test was found or cited. While `_config_schema.py` contains the validator (evidenced in criterion 12), no test asserting the rejection behavior with a specific error message naming the cleartext risk was identified.
findings.remediation: Provide evidence of a test that passes a non-`https` URL as `reconciler.base_url` (without `allow_insecure=True`) and asserts `ConfigError` is raised with a message naming the cleartext risk.
findings.title: No test found asserting non-https base_url raises ConfigError naming cleartext risk

findings.criterion: TLS certificate verification is never disabled — asserted against the parameter form the library
findings.detail: The evidence text ends with 'Now let me check the full test file for any test asserting that `allow_insecure=True` does not affect `options["verify"]`:' — no actual findings were reported. No test demonstrating that TLS certificate verification is never disabled (i.e., `options["verify"]` is never `False`) was identified.
findings.remediation: Provide evidence of a test that asserts `allow_insecure=True` does not set `options["verify"] = False` (or equivalent), confirming TLS certificate verification is always enabled regardless of the `allow_insecure` flag.
findings.title: No evidence of a test asserting TLS certificate verification is never disabled

findings.criterion: `reconciler.resolved_statuses` configures the DC absence-probe's resolved-status set, defaulting to
findings.detail: The evidence text ends with 'Now let me look for a specific test that covers both the default and custom resolved_statuses for the absence probe:' — no actual findings were reported. No test demonstrating that `reconciler.resolved_statuses` configures the DC absence-probe's resolved-status set (with default values) was identified.
findings.remediation: Provide evidence of a test that (1) verifies the default `resolved_statuses` value is used by the DC absence-probe, and (2) verifies a custom `resolved_statuses` value overrides the default.
findings.title: No evidence of a test for resolved_statuses configuring the DC absence-probe

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
